creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Learning graphs
Concept dependencies
Graph visualization
Knowledge mapping
dublinCore.description: Superseded first version of the learning graph viewer: 200 signal processing concepts and 370 prerequisite edges drawn with vis-network, Math Foundations pinned left and Applications and AI pinned right. Replaced by graph-viewer.

learningObjectives: Identify the taxonomy group of a concept from its node color and the legend
Trace a prerequisite chain by following arrows from a concept back to a Math Foundations node
Explain how fixed: { x: true, y: false } pins a node to a column while leaving it free to move vertically
Compare the number of arrows arriving at hub concepts such as Filtering and Signals with the number arriving at a typical concept to judge which concepts are most foundational
prerequisites: Familiarity with the course topic list

misconceptions.misconception: Arrows point from a prerequisite to the concept it unlocks
misconceptions.correction: In this graph the arrowhead is drawn at the prerequisite, so following arrows leads toward the basics
misconceptions.evidence: Follow Fast Fourier Transform to Discrete Fourier Transform, Fourier Transform, Fourier Series, Periodic Signals, Signals and Real Numbers

misconceptions.misconception: A node's horizontal position tells how advanced it is
misconceptions.correction: Only the pinned columns are placed by rule; all other positions come from the physics layout and vary between loads
misconceptions.evidence: Reload the page and compare the positions of unpinned nodes such as Unit Circle

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Interactive network of 200 signal processing concepts connected by 370 directed prerequisite edges, colored by taxonomy group. Math Foundations concepts are pinned to the left edge and Applications and AI concepts to the right edge.

controls.label: Legend toggle (hamburger icon)
controls.description: Hides or shows the legend sidebar so the graph can use the full width
